notes: Output quantization is one HalfAwayFromZero rounding of the exact fixed-point value at the MarketStats boundary (10 §4, R-3). The dp per field is in `fields`.

The Q3 rows are the spec's own table (measured with Node 20). `ts` is what TS emits, `rust` is the required native output; the difference is an intended model change (D08, 60 CL-4) recorded once in PARITY.md, never a conformance failure.

`scenario` gives one way to produce the exact unrounded pnl in a ts-compat session: a post-only GTC BUY that rests and is filled as MAKER (fee 0, 11 §4) on a later tick whose best ask is strictly below the limit (13 §5.1 WorstQueueCompat: BUY fills when best ask < limit). pnl = cash_end - starting + qty x payout (10 C4). ts-compat validates neither tick nor size precision (11 §4), so 1.5-share sizes and 0.535 prices are accepted.
Rows with id prefix `extra-` are the author's additional cases derived from the same rule; they are not in the spec table.

fields.spec: 10 §4; 21 §11: min(up, down) computed on micros before rounding
10 §4, R14: one rounding from the exact rational; null iff no BUY fill of that outcome

scenario.fill: MAKER BUY UP 1.5 @ 0.67 (post-only GTC rests, filled when best ask < 0.67)
scenario.derivation: cash_end - starting = -(0.67 x 1.5) = -1.005; UP pays 0; pnl = -1.005

vectors.cause: positive tie: both round away from zero; no difference
vectors.note: Author's case: shows the tie rule only differs for negative ties.

vectors.cause: below the half: magnitude rounds down
vectors.note: Author's case. 10 §4 third cause: a TS value with accumulated float error may arrive as x.xx4999..; in Rust the exact micros value decides, there is no accumulated error.

vectors.spec: 10 §4, 10 R-3 (a value already on the grid is not re-rounded)

vectors.note: Author's case: a negative value that rounds to zero is emitted as 0, never -0.
Author's case: BUY fills 1 @ 0.5 and 1 @ 0.5625 give sum(p x q)/sum(q) = 1.0625/2 = 0.53125 exactly; one HalfAwayFromZero step to 4 dp.

vectors.spec: 10 R14 (one rounding from the exact rational, no double rounding)
vectors.note: Author's case: BUY fills 1 @ 0.5, 1 @ 0.5 and 1 @ 0.6: sum(p x q) = 1.6, sum(q) = 3. The exact rational 1.6/3 = 0.5333... rounds to 0.5333; rounding the micros intermediate 0.533333 again gives the same here, but R-3 forbids the second step in general.
Author's case: JSON emission is plain decimal digits; no exponent, no f64 round trip.
Author's case: the emitted value has at most 2 fractional digits, below the decimal(14,4) column scale, so a fresh run and an --extend recomputed from DB decimals agree (Q1).
